node.title: B_C is an integer staircase: the adjacent crossing EXISTS; corridor = candidate list
node.statement: B_C(a) is nonincreasing and integer-valued in a, so a unique a* with B_C(a*-1) > B* >= B_C(a*) exists UNCONDITIONALLY for every row. The corridor arithmetic already brackets a* to at most ceil(width)+1 = 2-3 candidate grid points per rate. The endgame is therefore a FINITE list of pointwise decisions, not an analytic meeting of bounds.
node.notes: elementary; reframes adjacency_closing from 'no mechanism' to 'decide <= 3 points per rate' | IN FLIGHT: #193 | FLIP on replay (Codex wave 3): PROVABLE -> PROVED.
